column1: # verbs.tsv (harbor#1432) — the verbs of the `harbor` command: the script each dispatches to, whether it takes --json, and its note.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. contracts/cli.md held the verb table by hand and bin/harbor holds the same pairs embedded (a recovery command
# must not parse a markdown file, see cli.md), so lint.cli-contract compared two copies. The table in cli.md is now generated from this
# file (sh bin/standard-inventory.sh page cli --write, held current by contracts/fresh-checks.tsv); the equality with bin/harbor stays.
#   script   the bin/ file it dispatches to, with the fixed words after it (`deploy.sh --only floor`)
#   json     yes when the verb passes --json through, no when the dispatcher refuses it
#   notes    the cell of the table: markdown, a pipe written \|

column4: notes

the generated counts; `--json` is the machine form the dashboard consumes **THE SUITE COUNTS ARE CACHED ON CONTENT (2026-08-22).** `--apply` ran every counted suite to scrape one integer each, and `floor-test.sh` alone is **292s** of that — 1438 assertions at ~200ms apiece, because each fires a guard through ~110 process forks. Regeneration is not occasional: T1 and T1b fail on a stale docs/generated/status.md, so any commit touching a counted fact needs one, and at five minutes it gets backgrounded, killed, and left half-written — this tool dropped a `docs/generated/status.md.tmp.<pid>` twice in one session that way. A gate that slow is one people route around (§2.11). A recorded count is reused **only when the bytes it was measured against are unchanged**: the key hashes every `bin/*.sh` and `bin/*.awk`, not just the suite file, because "N passed" drops when a guard regresses, not only when an assertion is added. Cold 4:48 → warm **0.33s**, byte-identical docs/generated/status.md. It IS a relaxation of `suite_supplied`'s rule that no mode may rest on a number this process did not watch a suite print — a hit rests on a number an EARLIER process watched, against byte-identical inputs, recorded in gitignored `build/` so it never travels to another box claiming to be measured there. CI is unaffected: it supplies `HARBOR_STATUS_SUITE_COUNTS` from suites it ran in the same workflow, and that path is checked first. `tests/status/generate/generate.test.sh` covers the invalidation, which is the half worth testing **SUB-VERB `obligations` (harbor#1050).** `harbor status obligations [--json | --print | --since <N>s\|m\|h\|d]` is the obligations ledger's read side. The verb table above is frozen, so `bin/harbor` itself routes `status obligations` to `status-obligations.sh show` and every other `harbor status` call reaches `status-generate.sh` unchanged; `--json` on it is the shape in [`harbor status obligations --json`](#harbor-status-obligations---json) below, and not `status-generate.sh --json`
external dependencies, each row naming **what breaks**

answers "is the floor on?" for the live box by FIRING known-blocked shapes at `~/.claude`. The target is named by the verb's own `--live`, never implied by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (harbor#800); a sandbox is `sh bin/admission-verify.sh --dir PATH`

the **live tier** of the test contract ([test-contract.md](./test-contract.md) rule 6, harbor#735): "does the installed box work?" — floor-verify, doctor, install-drift, the shims, the roots and sec0's four decided `env` keys (harbor#816), one line each stamped `[check:deploy.live-verify]`, exit 1 if any is red. `--live` is required and `--dir` refused: a sandbox is a HOME. `--probes` adds the real-system probes harbor#667 moved behind stubs. **Read-only, and never in CI** (exit 2 under `CI`)

the conventions gate. Runs at `hooks/pre-push`, in CI (`governance.yml` job `conventions`) and via `just lint` — **not** in `pre-commit`, which runs the floor's smoke (`T_SMOKE=1 tests/admission/baseline/baseline.test.sh`) and the staged guards' table smoke (`T_SMOKE=1`, harbor#667) and nothing else; this cell said "also the pre-commit hook" until 2026-09-20. `--list` names every rule, `--only <ID>` runs exactly one. **An unknown id exits 2**, deliberately: selecting nothing and printing `0 violations` would be a clean report about a rule that never ran, the same false green `drift.renew-check`'s tokens exist to keep apart from "nothing is wrong". A whole-tree run costs ~115s and most single rules under a second, which is what makes a red-arm proof (§2.10) affordable per rule rather than per file
document + working-context staleness; `--open` for open markers
citation drift against `docs/reference/citations.md` (needs network)
the guard-decision ledger (OBSERVE-1)
render `build/dashboard.html`; `--open` to open it

harbor#457 — the ONE install command, and on the install standard the only live entry. **A verb since 2026-09-30, by an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table the operator approved explicitly**: `harbor deploy [args…]` passes every argument through, so the install runs from any directory, where `just deploy` / `just deploy-apply` (kept as aliases) need the checkout as cwd; deploy's own refusals hold through the verb (`tests/deploy/deploy/standard.test.sh`). The other `harbor` install verbs route here as `--only <component>`. Every installer onto this box, in the order that works (constitution → shim → sec0-harden → runtime → floor → prod-guard → skills → commands → inject → packs (the `packs` harbor.toml lists, through `bin/pack.sh`, harbor#1149) → skill-catalog → project-init's and projects-orchestrator's own `just install`, harbor#736). It owns order, preflight, snapshot and verify; every write is delegated to the installer that owns it. **Refused up front, before any check or plan**, under a Claude session with `--apply` or from a linked worktree, with the exact command to run in a terminal. **Preflight is read-only and refuses before the first write**: not the main checkout on a clean `main` equal to `origin/main`; `HARBOR_SCOPE_REPO` not this checkout; no `settings.json` in the config dir (its fix is the exact `harbor scope install` command, harbor#457); an install-stamp regression; a box B6 already blocks (the installers would re-pin over it); a box-only inject pack or skill file, a skill holding bytes in no commit, a shim over a regular file; any installer's own dry run failing, the other repos' `just install` included; **any component this run was asked for and cannot install** (project-init or projects-orchestrator unresolved, without an `install` recipe, or `just` not on PATH; prod-guard with no `prod_guard.py`), its fix this run with `--only` every selected component but those. They were `skip:` lines until 2026-09-30, and a new box reported "installed and verified" having installed only Harbor. **Opt-ins are read from the box** (harbor#762): a wired Stop gate and an installed B6 are refreshed; `--with-b6` / `--with-stop-gate` opt a box in, and `--with-b6` on a box with no floor is refused (B6 installs last). Then one `[y/N]`, a tar snapshot of everything the installers write (`.harbor-manifest` included) plus `local-bin.tsv`, a record of `~/.local/bin` that `deploy-restore.sh --live` puts links back from (harbor#770), the install (stops at the first failure and offers the snapshot back through `deploy-restore.sh`, then runs every check again on the restored box), and verify: B6 verdict, `install-drift` against HEAD, the dispatcher, `drift.reference-check`, each other repo's `just install --check`, `floor-verify`. **The B8 re-pin is asked last and stays the operator's**: it separates what THIS deploy changed from drift that predates it and defaults to No; EOF or no tty always answers No. That is an accident gate, not a wall: `script(1)` can fake a tty. **`--prune`** is the cleanup (§5): files the repo shipped and no longer ships (only when their bytes are a commit's), backups beyond the newest 10 per installer and 7 days, prod-guard's `settings.json.bak.*`, the retired baseline with `baseline-pin.sh` and its B6 pin together, a stale project-init bootstrap clone, dangling or double-owned `~/.local/bin` links — all MOVED into `backups/pruned-<TS>/` (a dry run unless `--apply`), and `pruned-*` dirs older than 30 days deleted. On the install standard: `[--apply] --live [--only C[,C…]] [--with-b6] [--with-stop-gate] [--prune] [--uninstall] [--accept-loss] [--unattended]` (`--unattended` is the ship runner's apply alone, harbor#1018: `HARBOR_DEPLOY_UNATTENDED=1` and an empty `$HARBOR_DEPLOY_SNAPSHOT` required, no install `[y/N]`, the snapshot id written to `$HARBOR_DEPLOY_SNAPSHOT`, No to the restore and the re-pin; [approval-gate.md](../docs/design/approval-gate.md); `--live` is required even for the dry run, `--dir` is a usage error: each installer takes `--dir` for a sandbox), its children run with `HARBOR_DEPLOY_ACTIVE=1` so they skip the next steps deploy performs (harbor#285), `--accept-loss` passes to constitution-, runtime-, floor- and skills-install and to `deploy-restore.sh`, and every `--apply` run keeps its log, children's lines, the restore and the re-check included, at `backups/deploy/<TS>/log`. **`--only floor --uninstall`** is `harbor uninstall` (harbor#808): the same refusals, `[y/N]`, snapshot and log, `admission-remove.sh`'s own dry run as the plan and as the verify that the floor is gone, and the snapshot offered back; every installed pack goes with the floor, and the skill catalog is regenerated without them.

installs the floor **through deploy**, the one live entry (the install standard §4, harbor#800): its preflight, snapshot, verify and restore offer. `--live` plans, `--apply --live` installs; a wired Stop gate and an installed B6 are refreshed, and `--with-b6` / `--with-stop-gate` opt in. **Ungated** — `eval-pass-score.sh` advises, and `grep -n pass-score bin/admission-install.sh` returns nothing. A sandbox is `sh bin/admission-install.sh --dir PATH`

removes the floor **through deploy** (harbor#808): an install's up-front refusals, preflight, `[y/N]`, snapshot and log. `admission-remove.sh`'s own dry run is the plan, and its verify: after the removal it must find no floor hook or file left, where floor-verify, B6 and install-drift would read every uninstall as a failure. A failed removal or verify offers the snapshot back through `deploy-restore.sh`; a clean one prints the `deploy-restore.sh --apply --live --from <snapshot>` that puts the floor back. `--live` plans, `--apply --live` removes. A sandbox is `sh bin/admission-remove.sh --dir PATH`
recovery: puts the config dir back from its newest deploy snapshot, or `--from` one (dry-run unless `--apply`; `--live` or `--dir PATH`). **The reason this is POSIX sh**

every tracked skill and slash command, installed **through deploy** (harbor#800): `--live` plans, `--apply --live` installs. One skill, or the listing, is `sh bin/skill-install.sh [<name>] (--live \| --dir PATH)`, which installs a tracked skill into `~/.claude/skills`. **Dry-run unless `--apply`** — it writes to an instruction surface the B8 pin watches. Verifies byte-identity after writing and refuses a nested `<name>/<name>/`, which the documented hand-typed `cp` produces silently. The target is `--live` or `--dir PATH`; the dry run exits 1 on what `--apply` would refuse, and `--accept-loss` is the one override (a newer live copy, box-only files; what it replaces goes into `backups/skills-install/<TS>/`). **`skill-catalog` is the one skill it composes instead of copying** (harbor#1149): the installed book lists every skill installed beside it and the box's CLIs, so the installer asks `skill-catalog.sh install --check` whether it is current, writes it with `skill-catalog.sh install --apply`, and puts it last in `--all`. Copying the tracked book over it would drop every row the repo does not ship

runs `context-injection-install.sh` **through deploy** (harbor#800): `--live` plans, `--apply --live` installs; `--projects` and `--remove` stay the installer's own, run directly. It wires the just-in-time injector into the box config, and seed each registered project's rule pack. **Dry-run unless `--apply`**, `--live` for the live config dir, and a **second** `--live` requirement on `--projects` because that flag writes into other repositories rather than into the target dir. `--remove` unwires, and moves the packs and the engine into `backups/inject-install/<TS>/` rather than deleting them. See [inject.md](./injection-rule.md)

runs `policy-constitution-install.sh` **through deploy** (harbor#800): `--live` plans, `--apply --live` installs. It deploys `policy/constitution.md` to the box's `CLAUDE.md` — the copy the harness actually loads, which nothing wrote to before this verb existed. **Dry-run unless `--apply`**, `--live` for the live file, and `--from-branch` on top of that for a non-`main` or dirty source, because a feature branch is text nobody has reviewed governing every future session. Prints the diff first, and the dry run runs every gate `--apply` does, the back-port loss check included (exit 1 if any would refuse; `--accept-loss` discards box-only text); never re-pins B8

which browser backend to use, and the verbs that drive it — `route`, `doctor`, `probe`, `hosts`, `cdp`, and `session` which is **declared and refused**. [browser-routing.md](./browser-routing.md) is the router; this verb `cat`s it rather than restating it. **THE VERB IS THE POINT (harbor#458).** The routing table lived inside one skill and nowhere else, so a session that had not loaded a measurement skill picked a backend by habit — and harbor#445 refused a browser capability on the opposite of what that table said. A capability reachable only by absolute path IS that defect, so this is a deliberate amendment to a frozen table, not an incidental one. Exit `0`/`1`/**`2` = SKIPPED**, taken verbatim from `doc-visual-check.sh`: no Node, no Chrome or no Playwright DEFERS and is never reported as a pass. `--self-test` proves each gate can fail offline; `--self-test-live` reproduces the one that needed a network — measured 2026-09-06, an anonymous run reported `meta` **ABSENT** on a page where accepting the consent banner turned up **39 more hosts** including Meta's tag host, so `hosts` now WITHHOLDS an absence verdict when a CMP loaded and nothing accepted it

router **row 4**: drives the operator's own Chrome through the Playwright Extension with a pinned `@playwright/cli` — attended (he clicks *Connect* on every attach) unless he registered the extension token `playwright-extension-token` in the access register, which `attach` alone uses; `hosts` prints the allow-list it reads, one browser session per Claude session, default-deny verbs and options, `https` vendor-UI hosts only ([browser-agent-hosts.txt](./browser-agent-hosts.txt)), bounded idle detach, and `doctor` for readiness. A separate verb rather than a `harbor browser` sub-verb so `access-browser.sh`, whose exit `2` means SKIPPED, is not forced onto `library-log.sh`, whose exit is 0 iff nothing failed (harbor#472)

harbor#996 (A2): every edge that touches a path or an id, read from `build/graph.tsv`, which `doc-graph-generate.sh` rebuilds first, so an answer never comes from a stale graph. A path is unqualified for harbor's own tree (`bin/admission-bash.sh`), `<system>:<path>` for fleet, yard and memory-store, and `~/…` for this box; an id is `check:<id>`, `log:<tool>`, `decision:D-<n>` or the bare id, and a bare `D-<n>` resolves to its decision. Seven edge types: `references` (a line holds the path as a literal substring), `deploys_to` (the install manifest, `~/.local/bin`, installed LaunchAgents), `derives_from` (a generated file's named generator), `emits` (`log_init`, `[check:<id>]`), and for decisions (harbor#1029) `defines` (a record's `alias:` line), `decided-by` (a line that cites `D-<n>`, whether or not a record defines it) and `revised-by` (a record's `revised_by:` line). A path's deployed copies are followed one hop, so the `~/.claude/settings.json` line that wires a guard is listed under the guard. `--sites` prints only the node's own-tree inbound sites as `path:line`, the shape `git grep -n -F <path> \| cut -d: -f1,2` prints, so the two diff to nothing (`tests/doc/graph-generate/graph-generate.test.sh`). **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#996 A2), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table.** Exit 1 when the graph holds no such node, 3 when python3 is absent. `doc-graph-generate.sh --dangling` (harbor#996 C2, not a verb) lists the manifest rows whose installed file is gone, one `<path> TAB <site> TAB <why>` each, builds no graph, and exits 1 when any; `drift-reference-check.sh` REF-5 folds each row in as a finding

harbor#996 (D2): `standard-catalog.sh` builds the catalog (`--census`, `--map`, `--check` are its own, run directly) and `harbor find <term>` lists what a family owns, one `kind<TAB>subject<TAB>detail` line each, in a fixed order: `script`, `test`, `check`, `doc`, `control`, then any other kind by its name. A path comes from the catalog (`sh bin/standard-catalog.sh --census` writes it as `build/catalog.tsv`); a `check` or `control` is a `controls.tsv` row owned by the family. The term is a family, a subsystem, a domain or a system, tried in that order; the first line names which. The catalog is rebuilt on every call from `git ls-files` and the registry, so an answer is never stale. Exit 1 when the term is none of them. **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#996 D2), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table.**

harbor#996 (D2): the seven levels of harbor/D-57 (`metasystem › domain › system › subsystem › family › component › element`, read from the `level` terms of `terms.tsv`) as a tree. A system's own files of kind level `system` sit on the system node, a family holds its component kinds and then its element kinds with counts (`controls.tsv` rows count as elements of their owner family), and files whose family the registry cannot name yet are one `unassigned` line. `harbor tree <term>` narrows to a domain, system, subsystem or family; `--files` lists the paths. Rebuilt on every call, like `harbor find`. **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#996 D2), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table.**

harbor#1043 (E1): the local append-only event bus, `${HARBOR_EVENT_DIR:-~/.local/state/harbor/events}/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` in UTC, one JSON line per event ([docs/design/events.md](../docs/design/events.md)). `emit <kind> <subject> [--src] [--repo] [--cause] [--data]` **always exits 0** and prints the id, so a broken bus never fails a hook, a commit or a CI job; `wait '<grep -E pattern>' --timeout N [--since-offset F]` sleeps on `tail -F` and exits 0 on the first match (printing it) and **3 at the deadline**, the one verb with a 3, because a deadline is a report and must not read as a usage error; `since <offset-file> [--consumer NAME]` prints the complete lines past a stored offset and advances it; `tail [N]`; `prune` deletes day files older than 14 days (docs/reference/checks.md `event.retention`). **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#1043), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table the operator signs at merge.** harbor#1044 (E2) adds four verbs that `event-bus.sh` hands to `bin/event-dispatch.sh`: `dispatch [--once]` follows the bus from its offset and runs the `on` rules (docs/reference/checks.md `event.dispatch`); `on '<pattern>' --id event.<object> … -- sh {cfg}/bin/<allowlisted script>` or `--spawn '<prompt>'`, and `on --preset|--list|--off`, refused unless docs/reference/checks.md registers the id with its trigger and disable command; `pull --session ID` or `pull --hook` prints one line of a repo's events since a session's last turn, or nothing; `subscribe` is **refused with exit 4**: the messaging socket is unverified. The security floor never depends on it

harbor#738 — the console: Harbor's live state as read-only panels on a localhost page. **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#738), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table the operator signs at merge.** `tools/ui/server.ts` on Bun, no framework and no dependencies, bound to `127.0.0.1` only. It prints one URL whose launch code works once: the first use is swapped for a separate random session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict) and a 303 to `/`, a second use is 403. It answers 403 to a request with no session, a foreign `Origin`, a foreign `Host`, or a `Sec-Fetch-Site` that is not `same-origin` or `none` (another localhost port is same-site, and cookies ignore ports), and stops after `--idle` seconds (default 1800) with no authorised request. **It runs only the commands in the one table in `tools/ui/sources.ts`**, each an argument array: a request names a panel id and never carries command text or a path, and an id outside the table is refused. A page load shows stored results and runs a source only when none is stored or it is older than `--min-age` (default 300s); `POST /run` and `POST /refresh` re-run, one process per panel at a time, and a source past its timeout is killed with everything it forked. Each panel names its source command and when it ran, and a source that fails or is absent renders `unavailable: <reason>`, never 0. Read-only: the page writes nothing, and re-running a panel re-runs its read command. Needs bun, which `harbor doctor` already reports. `--port N`, `--idle SECS`, `--wait SECS`, `--min-age SECS`, `--timeout SECS`, `--open`. Suites: `tests/status/console/guards.test.sh` (the guards, each with a red proof) and `tests/status/console/panels.test.sh` (the panels)

harbor#1060, harbor#1018 — the ship runner, built to ship contract v1.2 §3, §5, §5a and §5b: `night [--plan <file>]... [<owner/repo>...]` merges each opted-in fleet repo's ready PRs through `merge-stack`, one plan per PR pinned to the head it classified (`pr N head <sha>`; red skipped, protected queued, a moved head left for the next night), and deploys the default branch's change since the last deployed commit (`plan`, `apply`, every `verify`, each bounded by a timeout in its own process group; `restore` of this run's snapshot on red, on a timeout or on a signal, which stops the night); `deploy <owner/repo> --sha <sha> [--approved]` is one repo's deploy, `--approved` being `gate-approve.sh`'s alone and refused when `HARBOR_DEPLOY_UNATTENDED=1`. Opt-in, the manifest `.agents/ship.config` and the protected register are read from `origin/<default branch>`, never the working tree. Protected work is queued only through the installed `gate-queue.sh`; the classifier is the installed `gate-classify.sh`. The flow, the manifest and every rail: [docs/design/deploy-fleet.md](../docs/design/deploy-fleet.md). **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#1060, harbor#1018), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table the operator signs at merge.** Writes the per-repo deploy state, the report (`~/Deliverables/<date>-ship/REPORT.md`), one `[check:deploy.fleet]` line and its receipt. Exit 0 nothing failed (queued, skipped red, left for the next night and the kill switch are not failures), 1 a problem was reported, 2 a usage error, 143 a signal

harbor#1430, #1423 T18.7: creating or adopting a repo is one command. `harbor repo new <name> --kind <repo-kind> [--covers T] [--domain D] [--owner O] [--slug owner/name] [--remote URL] [--github] [--dry-run]` runs the scaffolder (`harbor yard new`), registers the repo (`repos.tsv`, #966), regenerates the project registry, routes memory to it, makes `context-rules/<name>/`, plans the label sync (#1427), runs the versions check (#1426), registers it with fleet and audits it. `harbor repo adopt <path>` is the same for a checkout that exists. `harbor repo list` prints where each repo is known (registry, `projects.tsv`, yard marker, fleet discovery) and `harbor repo audit <name>` re-runs the checks. `--github` is the one step that writes to GitHub (the label sync `--apply`); without it nothing leaves the machine. `harbor repo rename <old> <new>` (`scope-repo-rename.sh`, #966) is a dry run that names every place the id lives on this box (the registry rows, `fleet.yaml`, the session and memory dirs, `context-rules/<old>/`, pack ownership, PATH shims and console scripts, mentions in `bin/`); `--apply --live` moves the checkout, its worktrees and its session and memory dirs, runs `git worktree repair`, rewrites the rows and re-points the shims under their old names. The GitHub rename is printed as the operator's step and never run. Never reimplements the scaffolder or fleet: it dispatches to them. Exit 0 every step green, 1 a step failed or a check is red, 2 usage, 3 a step could not look

harbor#966, harbor#1149: `harbor scope install`, the first-install step. Creates the `PORT_ROOT` skeleton (`.worktrees/`, `.scratch/`, `history/`) and an empty private layer, `harbor-private/` (`harbor.toml`, a `repos.tsv` header, `access/`, `jobs/`, an empty `checks.md`, a `CLAUDE.personal.md` stub), the shape in [private-layer.md](./private-layer.md). **Idempotent:** it never overwrites or deletes, and prints `created` or `kept` per path; `--dry-run` prints `would create` and writes nothing; `--private-only` skips the `PORT_ROOT` skeleton. `--seed-from-projects` adds `repos.tsv` rows, for ids not already there, from the private layer's `projects.tsv` (`scope-roots.sh --projects`) and the git checkouts (a `.git` directory, a real remote) already under `PORT_ROOT`; remotes lose any `user:token@` part. `PORT_ROOT` and `HARBOR_SCOPE_PRIVATE` are read through `scope-roots.sh`. **It also seeds the config dir's `settings.json` as an empty `{}`, only when it is absent (harbor#457):** deploy's preflight refuses a box without one and a machine where Claude Code never ran has none. A present file (a symlink to one included), a dangling symlink, or a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` naming a dir other than `~/.claude` (deploy refuses that too) is left as it is and the line says so; `--private-only` skips it; whether a later first `claude` start keeps a pre-seeded file is UNVERIFIED, so the seed is one line to drop (`seed_settings` in `bin/scope.sh`) **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#966), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table the operator signs at merge.** Exit 0, 1 when no root resolves, 2 a usage error

harbor#1205, harbor#1149: the access register, one list of every identity an agent may use ([access-register.md](./access-register.md)). `add <id> --kind K --what T --use-when T --reaches T --cannot T --grant T (--secret REF \| --no-secret) [--value-stdin] [--probe CMD]` records an entry in `<private>/access/register.md`, then stores the value through `bin/secret` (stdin or its no-echo prompt, never an argument) and puts the register back if the store fails; `list`, `refs`, `has <ref>` (0 registered, 3 grandfathered in `contracts/secret-legacy-refs.txt`, 1 neither) , `check` (well formed, no credential-shaped value; exit 2 with no register, never a pass) and `stored` (every item `bin/secret` holds, by name: one no entry names is refused to its consumer, exit 1; exit 2 when the store cannot be listed). `status [-v\|--json] [id...]` is the lifecycle check (stored, alive, in date; exit 1 on any red, 2 when the store or register cannot be read); **`status --json` is the only form that takes `--json`** (harbor#1480; every other `harbor access` verb refuses it, exit 2): ONE object, `{ts, entries:[{id, kind, state, stored, alive, expires, days_left, problem, since}]}`, for the Harbor pane. `state` is `ok`, `dead`, `expiring`, `expired`, `unstored` or `unknown` (unprobed, undecided, held, unmanaged, n/a, revoked and a check with no verdict); `alive` is true or false only when a check ran and decided; `problem` is the text mode's reason on a red or expiring entry; `since` is the day that state was first seen. Names and states only: no credential value, no check output and no free-text field reaches it, and text mode is byte-identical. **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#1205), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table the operator signs at merge.** With no private layer the register is empty: `add` refuses, `has` is 1. `bin/secret` calls `has` before every verb that names a ref and refuses an unregistered one

harbor#1149, harbor/D-80, harbor/D-84: `list`, `install [<repo-id>...]` and `remove <repo-id>...` for the `harbor-pack/` folder of a workload repo; the pack.toml format, the five refusals, the install manifest and where files land are [pack.md](./pack.md). The target is chosen as every installer chooses it (`--live` or `--dir PATH`, dry run unless `--apply`, install-lib). A refused or incompatible pack is skipped by name and the run exits 1. `harbor deploy` runs it for the `packs` harbor.toml lists (after inject, before the skill catalog), and `harbor uninstall` removes every installed pack. **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#1149), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table the operator signs at merge.** Exit 0, 1 a pack was refused or a manifest is missing, 2 a usage error

harbor#1278 - the member laptop's and the admin's door to the company hub (`contracts/hub.md`). `init` checks what the laptop still needs (managed env, the admin's key in `hub-signers`, git, jq, ssh-keygen, a token) and syncs. `sync [--no-fetch] [--live \| --dir PATH]` fetches the signed policy (`hub-sync.sh`), installs the hub packs it pins from the hub clone at the pinned commit (`pack.sh --hub`, no gitleaks on the laptop), delivers the hooks it lists against their signed sha256 and prints the pin line. `status` shows role, hub, state, serial, mode, last sync, the pin against the installed core (a mismatch is shown and stays IT's until the updater exists), packs and hooks. `sign <policy.json> --key K` validates then signs with `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n harbor-hub`; `check [DIR]` and `pin-check <contract> [DIR]` are the admin's and the hub gate's checks (pin-check reuses the pack `harbor_version` grammar). `leave [--apply]` drops hub packs, hooks, policy and the clone on the agent side after a VERIFIED revocation only and names the root half as IT's step. `project register <name>` is `harbor repo adopt --core-only`: register, list and route a checkout with no yard, uv or just. `support list|accept <id>|connect <id>` is the admin's side of remote support (`hub-support.sh`, `docs/how-to/member-support.md`): your own `gh`, your own key, from a terminal of your own. Exit 0 done, 1 refused or a check is red, 2 usage, 3 the hub could not be reached (the last good policy stays)

harbor#1060 — merge a plan's PRs in order, squash only, each on its own green CI: `check <plan>`, `rehearse <plan> [--push]`, `merge <plan>`, `verify <plan>`; the procedure, the plan format and the trap each piece handles are [docs/design/merge-stack.md](../docs/design/merge-stack.md). **Added by the ticket's own spec (harbor#1060), an amendment to the CLI1-frozen table the operator signs at merge**; it is the first verb with a hyphen, so CLI1's and the dashboard's verb patterns now accept `[a-z-]+`. `check` writes nothing; `rehearse` writes only a scratch clone, and with `--push` one throwaway branch and its DO-NOT-MERGE PR; `merge` passes `--match-head-commit` with the head whose CI it judged, and `merge` and `verify` write what the procedure says and must run from a real Terminal (auto mode refuses a merge and a force-push). Exit 0 clean, 1 a problem was reported, 2 a usage error or a bad plan, 3 a pinned PR (`pr N head <sha>`) was on another head: `needs-rebase`, skipped and never synced. The plan names `repo`, `checkout`, `pr` lines in merge order, and optionally `workflow`, `tested` and `after N CMD`. The scripts never edit the plan. `gate-merge-check.sh` is the tool's own, not the repo's, so any repo can merge through it once it opts in: branch protection requiring checks, or `.agents/required-checks.tsv` where protection answers 403 (a 404 is refused by merge-check)
